title: Drop flat-vs-aisle detection from AddToShoppingListService
description:
Fixes a real-use defect found after the feature run. The original spec defined a flat-vs-aisle detection rule that returned 'flat' for empty/new lists (because they have no '## ' heading whose section contains a checklist item). This caused recipe-add on a fresh list to produce flat output with meal bullets interleaved between checklist items rather than the intended aisle-grouped output with all meal bullets at the top under '## Meals'.

The spec at specs/planned/add-to-shopping-list-from-recipe.md has been revised to remove the detection rule entirely. Both existing-list and new-list flows now always use aisle-aware appending. See in particular sections 'Append flow (existing list)' (step 6), 'Append flow (create new list)' (step 5), and the 'Edge cases' / 'Tests' sections.

What to change in code:
- CookbookApp/ShoppingLists/AddToShoppingListService.swift: remove the conditional that selected between flat and aisle-aware append. Always use aisle-aware append: appendItem(_:toAisle:) for non-nil aisle names, appendItem(_:) for the nil 'Other' bucket. Order of operations stays the same: read file, appendMealsBullet first (idempotent provenance bullet under ## Meals at the top), then iterate aggregated.aisles in their natural order, then within each aisle iterate items in order, calling the appropriate appendItem variant per item.
- CookbookAppTests/AddToShoppingListServiceTests.swift: drop any 'existing flat list, flat append' test. Replace with the test described in the spec's 'Tests' section under 'AddToShoppingListServiceTests': 'Existing list with hand-written flat items, items still go to aisle sections.' Also retain the 'Existing aisle-grouped list' test, 'Create-new flow' test, 'No aisle.conf' test, and 'Recipe scale applied' test, refreshing any of them where the language references the dropped detection rule.
- Run xcodegen generate in the worktree before xcodebuild to pick up any test-file additions.
- Verify build clean and all tests green.

Do not change CookbookCore. Do not change ShoppingListLineFormatter, AisleCatalog, RecipeScale, or the header view/extractor. The fix is localized to the service and its tests.
acceptance_criteria: AddToShoppingListService no longer detects 'flat' vs 'aisle-aware' mode. Both empty lists, new lists, and pre-existing lists (whether or not they contain hand-written flat checklist items) use the same aisle-aware append path.

For each AggregatedAisle in the aggregator output: for each AggregatedItem, format the line via ShoppingListLineFormatter.format(_:) and call list.appendItem(line, toAisle: aisleName) when aisle.name != nil, otherwise list.appendItem(line) for the nil 'Other' bucket. No conditional inspection of list.text drives this choice.

Items the user wrote outside any '## ' aisle heading remain in place — they are not rewritten or moved by this flow. The 0007 detail-view grouper continues to render them under the rendered 'Other' bucket.

Update AddToShoppingListServiceTests to drop any 'existing flat list, flat append' assertion and replace it with: 'existing list with hand-written flat items + recipe add → ## Meals + ## <aisle> sections appended; the hand-written flat lines remain verbatim where they were'.

Verify with the canonical scenario the user reported: a fresh '# Test shopping list' file → add Tiramisu → add Pizza → file ends up with '## Meals' (containing both '- **Tiramisu**' and '- **Pizza**' bullets) followed by aisle sections (## produce, ## dairy, ## pantry, ## bakery, ## flours, etc.) with each ingredient under its mapped aisle. No interleaving of meal bullets and checklist items.
